title: Differentiable Integer Linear Programming
abstract: Machine learning techniques have shown great potential in generating high-quality solutions for integer linear programs (ILPs), but supervised approaches require expensive solver-generated labels and may produce infeasible solutions. The paper proposes DiffILO, an unsupervised learning paradigm that reformulates discrete constrained ILPs as continuous, almost-everywhere differentiable, unconstrained optimization problems. This enables simultaneous problem solving and model training through gradient descent without traditional solver labels. Experiments on common ILP datasets report an average 13.2-times training speedup over supervised methods together with higher feasibility ratios and improved solution quality.
